For years, I've taken my pets to Dr. Jerry. He's treated some very difficult cases:
1. My hamster Gordita's cancer.

2. My 18-year-old cat, who was blind, deaf, and already had kidney damage.

3. When a kitten opened my Chihuahua Berenjena's iris.

4. When my cat Momili was poisoned.
These are just four of the biggest cases he's treated, but I've seen him perform other miracles. And yes, he saved them all.

Today, my kitten Silvestre died on the operating table at that veterinary clinic. Yes, he died, but you know what? Every time I saw him sick these last few days and told Jerry, he NEVER HESITATE TO SEE HIM, EVEN IF IT WASN'T HIS OFFICE HOURS. He always spoke to him gently, he always treated him, and above all, he tried to understand what was wrong. My cat stopped eating and started having diarrhea, passing mucus and then blood. I never stopped seeing him, caring for him, or communicating with us. He was only six months old, a baby. I don't want this pain in my heart to turn into hatred. I don't want all the love I feel for my cat to turn into hatred that makes me want to blame someone.

My heart is broken, and I want to tell Dr. Jerry in front of everyone how deeply grateful I am for all the time he gave me and each of my pets.

We couldn't do more for my little one, but from the bottom of our hearts, we did everything we could. The doctor even tried to resuscitate him several times and kept his heart beating long enough for me to see him that last time. He performed an autopsy, and we could see how bad he was despite all the care we gave him.

The pain made me try to find someone to blame, even myself, but the immense love I feel makes me realize I did the best thing by taking him to the most humane veterinarian of all.

Don't be fooled, don't let your judgment be clouded by opinions filled with pain and hatred.

Thank you so much, Vet. Silvestre and I owe you so much for everything you did for us. 🖤

Update: A few months ago, I rescued two kittens from the street. Unfortunately, both had littermate issues. He's currently treating my cat Petunia, who has an immune system disorder where her immune system attacks her. She has a severe form of feline acne. :( However, we're getting her through this thanks to Jerry. It's been a couple of weeks now, and she's improving a lot. ❤️

Jerry is the veterinarian who owns the shop—we've taken our tortoise there twice with great success!
Tortoises often suffer from eye infections—since they can't open their eyes, they can't eat because they can't see the food. The first time, Jerry gave him an injection, and he healed very quickly. He prescribed vitamins for his water and a diet of raw meat (except seafood) and all kinds of leaves and fruits (except citrus). This time, he came in dehydrated, so Jerry trimmed his nails and changed his diet back to what he had been doing before.

His fees are very reasonable, and he has extensive knowledge of non-furry animals.

I highly recommend him.

I took my turtle in because it hadn't eaten in several days. When we arrived, the vet left us waiting in his "waiting room," a truly disgusting and unhygienic place where everything was crammed together. He had several fish tanks with various reptiles, and I should have left right then and there, but I trusted the Google reviews.

When he examined my turtle, he did absolutely nothing. He just turned it over, looked at it for five minutes, and then handed it back to me, but not before scolding me for not treating my pet like an animal and worrying so much.

When I got home, my turtle died. If the vet had taken things seriously and really examined my turtle thoroughly, she would still be here.

Take your pets to a place where they truly make them feel comfortable, where they are thoroughly examined even if they appear physically healthy, and where you don't feel bad for trying to give them a decent life.

I DO NOT RECOMMEND HIM. I took my dog ​​to him for surgery, and she died yesterday.
I trusted him because of his "experience," but he performed a botched surgery. I don't know if he or the student made the mistake, which is unethical to ignore. He over-anesthetized her, and in the subsequent checkups, he was NEGLIGENT. He just kept saying it was strange that she was still unwell. She started vomiting blood, stopped eating, and he washed his hands, saying he hadn't touched her stomach. The next day, she woke up with a very swollen abdomen (it looked like it was going to explode), she was dehydrated, and she was still vomiting blood.

She got worse, so I took her to another vet. She arrived with hypothermia, a low heart rate, and was intoxicated from the urine that had already leaked into her system. The vet pricked her with a syringe to confirm that the swelling in her abdomen was indeed urine. They performed emergency surgery, and upon opening her up, they realized the incision in her bladder had been done incorrectly, and the sutures had been improper. The weight of the urine caused a stitch to come loose, which is why it leaked.
She came through the second surgery well; in fact, I thought she would recover quickly, but the damage was already done. My dog ​​was weak and stopped eating. It was a scheduled surgery, meaning my dog ​​was fine. I can't stop thinking that I rushed her so the anesthesia would take effect, never imagining that I was just taking her there to suffer.
Terrible service, negligence is rampant there. They let an intern perform surgeries alone without any supervision, and that's why a dog lost its life.

I highly recommend this veterinarian for his excellent care of cats. I took my cat for a checkup and was very satisfied with the service. The doctor was very kind and explained in detail that my cat had an infection. During the examination, he took her vital signs (temperature, heart rate, and respiration), palpated her, and asked me a series of questions about the symptoms, when they appeared, her medical history, and her habits.
To treat her, he administered three injections and prescribed an oral antibiotic. He also gave me clear instructions for administering the medication at home and explained the warning signs that would indicate the need for an immediate consultation.
The veterinarian also gave me recommendations to improve my cat's quality of life, including alternatives for brushing and her overall well-being.
A few days later, noticing that my cat was licking herself excessively and had developed considerable irritation and inflammation, I returned for another appointment. The veterinarian applied an anti-inflammatory ointment and gave me enough to continue the treatment at home.
The cost of the consultation and treatments is affordable. The veterinarian's commitment to pets is evident, as, in addition to providing quality care, he strives to help owners objectively understand what is happening to their animals and avoid feeling overwhelmed by uncertainty.
The clinic is open in the late afternoon and evening. There is no on-site parking, but it is available nearby. They accept cash payments and can be contacted via the phone number displayed on their sign.
